cells.tense: What is yours to give is already here and already moving through you.
cells.act: name the mechanism in one line and change nothing
cells.ask: Catch the shape you keep falling into with the people closest to you, put it in a single plain line inside your own head, and change nothing about it today.
cells.core:
You can be fully yourself around people without turning it into a performance. When you feel with someone, you don't dim to match them and you don't brighten to lead them. The shine is just what's there when nothing is being managed — warmth that doesn't need a reason.

Left alone, that radiance tends to get explained. You start reaching for the why of it, or for the one more thing it should become. Next time you notice how you show up for someone — the same shape, again — put it into one plain line inside your own head, and then let it be. That sentence is the whole practice. What's already lit doesn't need the commentary.
cells.sheetLine: You shine around people without needing to prove it.
cells.place: where you feel with people, near or far

cells.tense: The light is being aimed before you have felt whether anyone is ready for it.
cells.act: leave it undecided a while longer
cells.ask: When you have already settled what someone needs, hold it open a while longer. Not buried — just not given yet. See what they bring first.
cells.core:
You can be so ready to give that you get there before the moment does. The warmth is real, but it comes with a plan attached, and the plan gets handed over before the person has said what they actually need. What's already bright starts announcing itself, and the people nearby step back instead of leaning in.

Try letting the next thing stay open. Someone brings you a problem, and you have the answer — keep it unanswered for now. In that gap you find out what they were going to say on their own. Your light doesn't go anywhere when it waits. Open and available, it lands better than aimed.
cells.sheetLine: You hand over the light before anyone asked for it.
cells.place: where you feel with people, near or far

cells.tense: What you already became is still standing at a door it has walked through.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Choose one of two things that are yours — this, not that — and do the first real thing it asks, with someone nearby knowing which way you went.
cells.core:
Something in you has gone quiet that didn't used to be. Around people, you hold back the part that would have shown — not out of modesty exactly, but as if the glow were an old coat you no longer reach for. Where you feel with others, you stay one step back, giving the moment to whoever else is in it.

The return isn't to feel more connected on command. It's to pick. Name a direction that is yours — a thing you want, a way you want to show up — and do the first real thing it asks, with someone nearby knowing which way you went. Direction pulls the current through. Connection follows a choice, not the other way around.
cells.sheetLine: You dimmed what you already became and called it modesty.

cells.tense: You are already shining and the story you tell about it keeps leaving you out.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: While someone opens up to you, catch the small thing happening in you as it happens — the pause, the listening — not afterward.
cells.core:
People leave your company warmer than they came, and if asked, you'd say you didn't do much. The thing that happens around you happens through you, and it has no author in your account — the shine is real, and the one who shines keeps getting left off the page.

It can stay unnamed. But try catching one moment while it is happening. Someone tells you something hard, and you meet it exactly as it is, nothing prepared. In the middle of it, catch the small thing you do — the pause, the listening, the half-sentence. That catching is the whole return. Not pride — just seeing yourself in the turning, where you already are.
cells.sheetLine: The light is yours and you keep leaving yourself out of the story.
cells.place: where you feel with people, near or far

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is in Too Much: that reaching to organise or inspire is blinding the people nearby — the record supports excess radiance, not that others are actually dazzled. A reader could reasonably say they are simply tired or overextended, not inflating. The ask survives being wrong either way: leaving something undecided for one day costs nothing and teaches something regardless of the diagnosis. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line implying the person has been performing for an audience — that is inference, not record, and it stays out of the glass.
